subject: Cross type query - forming a map.

messages.author: d18738ddff11a439
messages.subject: Cross type query - forming a map.
parts:
Hi Karl,

I'm following the "Genetic map construction wit R/QTL" PDF to create a genetic map for QTL analysis using R/QTL.
I have a biparental tetraploid wheat mapping population which was selfed to F4. I have around 2380 markers and 104 individuals.
I've got towards the end of the steps in the PDF, but have realised that I may have been using the wrong cross type. Following my data format: AA, AB, BB - my cross type was automatically assigned as " F2 intercross" as I didn't specify anything in the read.cross command.

Firstly, What should I use in the read.cross command to account for the type of population and specify that it's F4?

Secondly, does this correction matter at this stage? or do I need to go back to the start and redo the ordering due to the potential change in cross.type?

Lastly, I've noticed that my ordered chromosomes appear slightly longer than comparisons using existing maps (on average 338cM - but some just over 400cM). My orders mostly look correct with comparisons. I still have gaps in places - on average my largest gap on each chromosome averages at 40cM. My marker number seems to large to use Ripple and I've tried using compare.order, droponemarker, est.map and dropped genotype errors. Any advice on how to tighten things up?

Really appreciate your time.

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Cross type query - forming a map.
parts:
R/qtl doesn't have a cross type appropriate for an F4 population. F2 might work okay for marker order, provided that you have little missing genotype data, but the maps are going to be expanded due to the multiple generations of recombination.

If there's little heterozygosity, you could try using "riself", but this would omit any heterozygous genotypes.

read.cross() has an argument 'crosstype' that you can use to specify the cross type.

If you switch cross type, I wouldn't start over completely; your current working marker order is likely a reasonable starting point.

karl
